name: ko-and-media
title: Knockout and media perturbations on the baseline whole cell
question:
How do a translation-level gene knockout (lacY) and an amino-acid-rich medium
each move the v2ecoli baseline off its wild-type trajectory — and how do you
express each as a one-line variant of the baseline composite?

report.evidence_quality: 1500-step single-cell run of all three arms, seed 0
report.result:
Dry mass over 1500 steps (see the Growth comparison figure):
- wild-type:  380.62 -> 547.69  (+43.89%)
- lacY-KO:    380.62 -> 547.69  (+43.89%)  — BYTE-IDENTICAL to wild-type.
    The knockout reaches the live PolypeptideInitiation process (exactly one
    translation efficiency zeroed = lacY) but is phenotypically SILENT in
    glucose-minimal (lac operon not needed): the two trajectories overlap
    exactly. The intended demonstration — the mechanism reaches the process
    without confounding growth.
- rich-media: 380.62 -> 559.47  (+46.99%)  — grows faster.
    minimal_plus_amino_acids diverges above the minimal arms from ~step 450;
    amino-acid-rich medium relieves biosynthetic demand. In-cache media shift,
    no ParCa re-fit.

findings.statement: baseline(knockouts=['EG10526']) zeroes exactly the lacY translation efficiency on the live process; growth is unchanged in glucose-minimal (correct — lacY is dispensable without lactose).

baseline(media='minimal_plus_amino_acids') reaches +46.99% dry mass vs +43.89% for minimal over 1500 steps (diverges from ~step 450) — the in-cache media shift takes effect via media_update without a ParCa re-fit.

variants.name: lacY-knockout
variants.expected_contrast:
lacY protein is no longer synthesised (its translation efficiency is zeroed
on the live PolypeptideInitiation process). In glucose-minimal this is
phenotypically near-silent — the lac operon is not needed — which is the
point: it shows the knockout mechanism reaches the process without
confounding the demo with a growth collapse. Swap in a gene the condition
needs to see a phenotype.

variants.name: rich-media
variants.expected_contrast:
An amino-acid-rich medium relieves biosynthetic demand, so the cell grows
faster than on minimal (verified: higher dry-mass accumulation over a short
run). A lightweight in-cache media shift — the media_update step applies the
condition on tick 1; no per-condition ParCa re-fit.
